$comment: ENC-17 shared golden vectors for the virtual rotary-encoder harness.
READ BY TWO THINGS, WHICH IS THE POINT:
(decodes these frames with the shipped RotaryEncoderDecoder)
If the harness's byte layout ever drifts from the decoder's, one of those two fails.
That matters here specifically: design/INTEGRATIONS.md documented a wrong 8-byte
encoder format for months, and nothing mechanical caught it.
'hex' is the full 37-byte Input Report 0x01 including the leading report ID.

'reportLength' is 107 because that is what the real device reports: HidSharp's GetMaxInputReportLength() is the maximum across ALL input report IDs, and the config read-back report 0x02 (106-byte payload + 1 report ID) is larger than the 37-byte positions report. Measured on the appliance 2026-09-03, and confirmed in the service's own log line 'Encoder report length 107 bytes (movement accumulators: true)'. BeginConnection only needs >= 37 to enable movement, so this also proves the decoder uses >= rather than ==.

positionReports.name: baselineZero
positionReports.note: The first frame of a connection. Absorbed as a baseline, never as input.

positionReports.name: volumeTwentyDetentsUp
positionReports.note: Twenty units of movement. The host clamps volume to 6 per event (ENC-3).

positionReports.name: accelerationTierByteSet
positionReports.note: Tier byte is reported but the host does not act on it; movement already includes acceleration.

positionReports.name: accumulatorWrappedToInt32Min
positionReports.note: One unit past INT32_MAX. Two's-complement subtraction must yield +1, not -4294967295.

positionReports.name: accumulatorAfterFiftyOfflineDetents
positionReports.note: Designer's re-baseline test: fifty detents accrued while nothing was listening.

decodeSequences.name: SteadyStateTurnProducesTheDelta
decodeSequences.description: Ordinary operation: baseline first, then each report's delta is the difference from the previous accumulator.

steps.note: First report of the connection: absorbed, produces no movement.
1 -> -3 is a delta of -4. Deltas are differences, not absolute values.

decodeSequences.name: ReconnectAfterFiftyOfflineDetentsDeliversNoJump
decodeSequences.description: ENC-1, Designer's highest-weighted test, verbatim: 'Turn a knob ~50 detents while unplugged, then replug: volume does not jump.' The accumulator is free-running, so a host that differenced against its last remembered value would deliver all fifty detents at once, on the volume knob. BeginConnection must discard the first report of the new connection.

steps.note: A normal turn before the disconnect, so the decoder is holding a non-zero last value.
The unplug and replug. Everything between here and the next report is the knob being turned with nobody listening.
THE ASSERTION. Fifty units of accrued movement arrive and produce zero delta.
And the connection is live again immediately: the next real turn produces a real delta measured from the new baseline.

decodeSequences.name: AccumulatorWrapProducesTheShortDelta
decodeSequences.description: The accumulator wraps at 32 bits rather than saturating, and the decoder subtracts unchecked so two's-complement gives the correct signed delta straight across the boundary. A saturating design would have frozen the control after ~119 hours of continuous fast spinning.

steps.note: INT32_MAX -> INT32_MIN is one unit forward, not 4294967295 units backward.

decodeSequences.name: RepeatedIdenticalReportsProduceNoMovement
decodeSequences.description: The harness's `idle <s> <hz>` mode re-emits an unchanged report. A device that repeats itself must not be read as movement.

decodeSequences.name: ButtonTransitionsAreEdgesNotLevels
decodeSequences.description: The decoder reports a button change only on transition, so a held button does not re-fire. EncoderLongPressGesture depends on that: a repeated press edge must not stack timers.

decodeSequences.name: AllFourEncodersDecodeIndependently
decodeSequences.description: Index order is VOLUME 0, SOURCE 1, PRESETS 2, TUNING 3, and the four accumulators are read from distinct offsets.
